That the patient missense alleles release cytochrome c has not been shown directly; the link to the disease allele is that it fails to rescue the knockout.

nodes.description: Ile311 and Tyr314 sit where the two UQCRC1 monomers of the complex III homodimer meet. In silico modelling on the published human complex III structure predicts that p.Ile311Leu alters the packing of neighbouring side chains and that p.Tyr314Ser removes an aromatic ring and disturbs van der Waals packing, so that both destabilise the homodimer. This step is a structural prediction: the discovery report did not measure complex III assembly or abundance in patient or model tissue.

meta.association: Heterozygous UQCRC1 missense variants cause autosomal dominant parkinsonism with polyneuropathy. The gene encodes core protein 1 of mitochondrial respiratory chain complex III, a subunit of the complex III homodimer. The founding variant p.Tyr314Ser (c.941A>C) and p.Ile311Leu (c.931A>C) co-segregate with disease in two Taiwanese families; a Japanese family (C) carries a splice/frameshift allele whose segregation could not be tested. All three alter residues conserved across species.

nodes.description: Heterozygous p.Tyr314Ser or p.Ile311Leu alters a conserved residue at the complex III homodimer interface. In silico structural modelling predicts both substitutions destabilise the homodimer, and because UQCRC1 carries no Q-cycle catalytic activity the effect is on complex stability rather than on a lost enzymatic function. The discovery report proposes a dominant-negative action on the homodimer; that is a hypothesis, and the later association of protein-truncating variants with Parkinson disease would instead fit haploinsufficiency, so the functional impact category is recorded as unknown.

nodes.description: Human SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells carrying heterozygous CRISPR/Cas9 knock-in of p.Tyr314Ser, p.Ile311Leu or the Family C splice allele, differentiated with retinoic acid. They show shorter neurites, lower maximal respiration and ATP production, more reactive oxygen species and a selective complex III deficit, most marked for p.Tyr314Ser. Later studies used the same cell model to show reduced induced mitophagy and, in a preliminary report, restoration of complex III-linked respiration by the beta-2 agonist formoterol.

evidence.reference_title: Formoterol Acting via β2-Adrenoreceptor Restores Mitochondrial Dysfunction Caused by Parkinson's Disease-Related UQCRC1 Mutation and Improves Mitochondrial Homeostasis Including Dynamic and Transport.
evidence.snippet: Mitochondrial function, encompassing DNA copy number, repatriation, and complex III-linked respiration, was comprehensively restored, along with the dynamic rebalance of fusion/fission events.

nodes.description: Human wild-type or p.Tyr314Ser UQCRC1 was expressed on a heterozygous Drosophila UQCR-C1 null background to mimic the human heterozygous state. Mutant flies show age-dependent locomotor decline, shortened lifespan, loss of TH-positive dopaminergic neurons, and reduced neuromuscular-junction bouton numbers, without alpha-synuclein pathology. The endogenous fly gene is knocked out and a human transgene supplies the variant, so the model acts through the human allele on the fly ortholog's null background.

Heterozygous CRISPR knock-in of the human p.Tyr314Ser substitution into the mouse Uqcrc1 gene. Mice are normal to 9 months, then develop progressive locomotor and gait deficits, nigral dopaminergic neuron loss, striatal dopamine deficiency, reduced complex III activity in nigra and striatum, sciatic nerve fibre degeneration and abnormal mitochondrial ultrastructure; motor deficits improve with levodopa. No alpha-synuclein pathology was detected.
